newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer-no full TARGET access for non-EMU banks.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer-no full TARGET access for non-EMU banks.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer on Monday repeated the Bundesbank's view that European central banks whose currencies do not join the future single currency should not gain unlimited access to the TARGET payment system.

In a speech to a political forum in Bonn, Tietmeyer said that such central banks should not be given unlimited access to intraday credits, but should only be given access to these on the basis of its credit holdings.
"It is not just or sensible to treat unlikes alike," Tietmeyer said.

The Bank of England has objected in strong terms to plans to limit its access to the planned wholesale payments system for the Euro, saying that restrictions placed on its access will disadvantage London as a financial centre.
But several European nations have argued that this is an unacceptable demand from Britain -- which is likely to opt out of a single currency in the first round.
In his speech, Tietmeyer said it had to be made clear that countries could not pick and choose what they wanted from the array of advantages the new single currency, the Euro, will bring.
"There cannot and must not be a 'Euro a la carte'," he said. "For that reason there can be no misinterpretation."

One of Germany's main objections to full participation by non-EMU banks in TARGET is that this would allow them to create liquidity in Euros, which could undermine the price stability policies of the future European central bank.

"A central bank, which does not take part in the currency union, and thus retains monetary policy sovereignty for its own national currency, cannot create liquidity in Euros from nothing," Tietmeyer said.
